summary: SCOPED CLAIM — the REVIEW TOOL ITSELF: services/control-plane/tower-loop/gitEvidence.mjs and reviewDiff.mjs. READ THIS FIRST, BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT IS AT STAKE. These two modules are the instrument that has produced every other verdict in this phase's review gate, and gitEvidence.mjs HAS NEVER BEEN INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED — I discovered that while auditing which parts of the diff had been gated, and it is the reason this packet exists. gitEvidence.mjs applies the pathspec, enforces the 60,000-byte diff cap, and sets the diff_truncated flag. Every claim of the form 'reviewed untruncated' that I have banked in this phase rests entirely on that flag being correct. If it is wrong, the verdicts it certified are unfounded — including the ones that approved other parts of this same teardown. It is the control that certifies the controls, and it went ungated because it was the thing doing the gating. WHY THE TOOL EXISTS AT ALL. Its predecessor, demo-merge-review.mjs, stages a REAL diff but hard-codes the throwaway demo's CLAIM. Pointed at real work it faithfully reviews a real diff against a fabricated, unrelated claim: observed 2026-08-02 returning request_changes, HIGH, BLOCKS_CURRENT_MERGE, refuting a CSV-converter claim nobody had made. The verdict was literally true and entirely meaningless — and the same mechanism could as easily have produced a FALSE GREEN over real work nobody actually reviewed. reviewDiff.mjs replaces exactly one thing, the fabricated claim, and adds no new review logic; it reuses gatherGitEvidence for evidence and runMergeReview plus the approved Tower QA skill for the review. WHAT CHANGED IN gitEvidence.mjs. Pathspec support was added because without it a large change could not be scoped and any diff over the cap truncated SILENTLY — which had already caused a review of this very teardown to return 'approve' with 20/20 rows over a diff the reviewer had only partly seen. The pathspec is applied to BOTH git invocations, deliberately, so that changed_files and diff_text always describe the same file set; a scoping option applied to one but not the other would let a packet claim coverage it does not have, which is the same defect class the module exists to prevent. WHAT I HAVE VERIFIED MYSELF, and it is not independent review: the cap fires correctly in both directions on real inputs (a 63,700-byte diff returns truncated=true, a 52,713-byte diff returns truncated=false), the reported byte counts match independent measurement, and changed_files exactly equals the set of files appearing as +++ headers in diff_text for a two-file scoped packet. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: neither module has any test file of its own — this is an untested surface, and that is a limitation of the packet, not something to be inferred from its absence. Nothing here has run in CI beyond the repo's existing control-plane job. The Codex invocation path (supervisorCodex.mjs, codexAdapter.mjs) is NOT in this packet and is not claimed. All evidence is my own execution. It is NOT independent review, which is what you are being asked for.
brief_excerpt:
Judge this diff against these criteria and ONLY these.

SCOPE. This packet contains services/control-plane/tower-loop/gitEvidence.mjs and reviewDiff.mjs ONLY. Rows about any other file are OUT OF SCOPE — mark them not_applicable, never blocked. supervisorCodex.mjs and codexAdapter.mjs are NOT here and are not being claimed. Neither module in this packet has a test file at all; do not report tests as missing from the packet, and do not treat their absence as evidence either way — it is disclosed above as a real limitation.

THE STAKE, so you can calibrate severity correctly. This is the instrument that produced every other verdict in this review gate. A defect here does not merely affect this packet — it retroactively undermines the verdicts the tool has already certified. Judge it as measuring equipment, not as application code. The question behind every row is: can this tool tell a reviewer it saw something it did not?

T1. TRUNCATION MUST NEVER BE SILENT. The diff is capped at MAX_DIFF_BYTES. Verify that whenever the cap is applied, diff_truncated is set to true and cannot be false while content has been dropped. Find any path where content is omitted, shortened, or altered without the flag being set. This is the highest-severity row in the packet: a truncated diff reported as complete is a reviewer approving ground it never examined, which is the exact failure this whole phase is treating.

T2. THE PATHSPEC MUST APPLY TO BOTH GIT CALLS, ALWAYS. changed_files comes from one git invocation and diff_text from another. If a scope reaches one but not the other, the packet claims a file set it did not deliver — or delivers content it did not declare. Verify they cannot diverge for any input, including an empty pathspec, a pathspec matching nothing, a pathspec matching a directory, and a pathspec containing a path that does not exist.

T3. FAIL-CLOSED ON UNRESOLVED EVIDENCE. An unresolvable range, a failed git call, or a missing base must produce a blocker rather than an empty-but-plausible evidence object. An evidence packet that is empty because git failed must never be indistinguishable from one that is empty because nothing changed.

T4. THE CLAIM CAN NEVER BE ABSENT OR EMPTY. reviewDiff.mjs exists specifically because its predecessor reviewed real diffs against a fabricated claim. Verify a missing claim file, malformed JSON, an absent summary, an absent brief_excerpt, and a whitespace-only value in either field ALL exit non-zero before any review is invoked. Reviewing against no claim must not be reachable by omission — that is the defect the module was written to make impossible.

T5. THE PACKET MUST NOT BE AUTHOR-CONTROLLABLE BEYOND THE CLAIM. Everything except the five claim fields is supposed to come from real git evidence and never from author input. Verify no path lets the caller inject or override the diff, the changed file list, the SHAs, or the truncation flag. The tool's entire value is that the DIFF is real even when the claim is the author's — if the diff is author-influenceable, the tool provides no assurance at all.

T6. REPORTED VALUES MUST MATCH DELIVERED CONTENT. The printed byte count, the SHA pair and the changed-file list must describe what was actually placed in the review packet, not what was requested. A record that cannot be trusted about what it reviewed is not a durable record however good the verdict.

ADVERSARIAL ROWS — answer even if every row above passes.
W1. Construct a concrete input where a reviewer would be shown LESS than the tool reports having shown it. Name it precisely.
W2. Can the cap interact with the pathspec such that a scoped review silently truncates while appearing scoped-and-complete? Scoping exists to AVOID truncation, so a scope that still truncates without saying so is the most dangerous combination available.
W3. Is there any input for which the tool exits ZERO having reviewed nothing, or having reviewed something other than what it reported?
W4. Binary files, file renames, mode-only changes, deleted files and files with CRLF line endings all appear in real diffs here. Does any of them break the byte accounting, the file list, or the truncation logic? Note that a CRLF-vs-LF discrepancy has ALREADY caused a real measurement error in this project, so treat line-ending handling as a live concern rather than a theoretical one.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not report as defects: the value chosen for MAX_DIFF_BYTES (a policy decision, and deliberately not raised to make a review fit); prose, naming or comment-style preference; the absence of test files, disclosed above; the Codex invocation path, which is not in this packet; and the absence of malicious-handler hardening, since this estate's bar is correctness, accidental leak, availability and audit for a first-party personal system rather than a hostile-input service. The threat model here is an honest operator being misled by their own instrument, NOT an attacker crafting a malicious diff.
